title: Divine Strength in Weakness
english: The word of power is that my strength is perfected in weakness.
When a famine was pressing upon the sons of Israel, they dwelled in Egypt in seventy-five souls, where their race was extended to a greater multitude, as it is written (Genesis 46:27).

The ruler of the Egyptians, however, did not suspect the multitude of the Hebrews and plotted against them, setting over them taskmasters of works to afflict them in the works, which included the sweat of digging and long and unpaid brick-making, as well as the building of fortified cities for Pharaoh, including Pithom and Rameses, and other cities.

It is said that in the humiliation of those punished in pride, the example was in greater ones, and they became more numerous, because God, wanting to benefit those unjustly insulted, was accustomed to use evil, and the tyrant's consideration was around the unexpected.

The tyrant, having understood the situation, devised another plot to add to the troubles of the Hebrews, ordering the Jewish midwives to suffocate the male babies and spare the female ones, as he believed the males to be useless and cowardly, in order to destroy the nation that was suspected of them.
The midwives, however, refused to obey this wicked command and instead pleased God.

The tyrant, enraged by their disobedience, ordered his people to throw every son who is born to the Hebrews into the Nile and to save every daughter alive, saying, "Every son who is born to the Hebrews you shall cast into the Nile, but every daughter you shall keep alive" (Exodus 1:22).
Let us pause the story here and consider the deeper meaning.

The human mind, inclined to evil from youth and lacking the good things from above, destroys the human race, and a kind of heavenly famine, like a devouring force, consumes us, as if we would neglect our duties…

The translation of 'ἐπίστατας τῶν ἔργων' as 'taskmasters of works' is preferred over 'supervisors of the works' because it more accurately conveys the genitive phrase indicating the type of taskmasters.
The allusion to Genesis 46:27 is based on the mention of 'seventy-five souls', which is the number of people who went down to Egypt with Jacob.
The sentence in paragraph 8 is incomplete, but it appears to be a numerical notation (γʹ) and does not affect the translation.
The translation of 'ἐγκειμένης' as 'lying' may not be entirely accurate, but it is the closest approximation in this context.

title: Moses as a Prefiguration of Christ
english: The resurrection of Christ is symbolized by the opening of the ark and the discovery of the crying child, demonstrating that he has come to life and trampled death.
Through faith, the Church has recognized and believed that Christ has died for us and given us life, just as those who found him through faith have truly believed.

We will also recount the wickedness of the Jews towards Christ, and the events that occurred, while telling and weeping, for it is written: They have pierced my hands and feet, and counted all my bones (Psalm 22:16-18).
They have looked at me and divided my clothes among themselves, and cast lots for my garment.
Additionally, it is written: They gave me gall for food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar (Psalm 69:21).
The Church from the Gentiles has recognized and believed that Christ has come from the Jews, as the daughter of Pharaoh said: This is one of the Hebrew children.
At the proper time, the synagogue of the Jews will receive Christ through the initiatory voices of the Church, having been initiated into the mystery that is on him.
This is not unworthy, for the synagogue of the Jews, having previously cast out Jesus and rejected him due to disobedience, will finally receive him.
The matter is not without profit, but is full of great hope, and is now assured, for the daughter of Pharaoh promised rewards to the mother of Moses, who was taking care of the child.
The birth and life of Moses clearly signify the mystery of Christ to those who are simple-minded, demonstrating the gentleness of divinity and the sinless one.
Through Christ, God and the Father are glorified with the Holy Spirit, now and forever.
As we investigate the birth of Moses, we see that it reveals the mystery of Christ, who is described in a newly born infant, showing that a new creation has appeared.
Let us consider again how Emmanuel is formed in Moses, for Christ is the end of the law and the prophets.

Moses, having become great, went out to his brothers, the sons of Israel, and saw their labor; he saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers, and struck the Egyptian, hiding him in the sand.
On the second day, he saw two Hebrew men quarreling and said to the one doing wrong, 'Why do you strike your neighbor?' The man responded…

title: Spiritual Discernment
english: By using an unforced mind, we will be able to discern the truth without any obstacles. When individuals are deceived by demonic forces, they often pursue what seems right to them, expending their own energy on these endeavors. The story of Jethro's daughters drawing water, while others seize it by force, presents a puzzling scenario that requires interpretation. Those who have been led astray are plagued by weaknesses that distort their innate knowledge, leading them down a path of error and usefulness to demons.

Fortunately, Christ has come to our aid, providing guidance and support in times of need. He rebuked the false shepherds and offered the living water of his divine and heavenly proclamation, as stated in john 7:37. Christ's invitation to those who thirst is clear: if anyone desires to drink, they should come to him. Jethro can be seen as a symbol of the world, which is characterized by excess and luxury. The seven daughters of Jethro represent the flocks of the nations, with each daughter signifying a multitude. The evil and violent shepherds can be reasonably associated with demonic crowds.

Christ, who intoxicates us with divine drinks, has come to our aid, providing a refuge from the forces of darkness. After escaping the greed of the wicked shepherds, the girls fled to their father Reuel, also known as Jethro, seeking safety and protection. When Jethro inquired about the reason for their haste, they immediately told him about Moses' help, expressing their gratitude. Jethro welcomed Moses and gave him his most prominent and beautiful daughter, Zipporah, to marry, and she bore Gershom.

Christ helped the systems of the world, and those who were saved through him recognized his ability to defend and rescue them from harm. Just as Raguel did with Moses, Christ adds his pleasure, demonstrating his delight in those who are saved. This union can be seen as a kind of intimacy between Christ and the Church from the nations, with the Church being presented as a beautiful bride, symbolized by Zipporah. The name Zipporah can be interpreted as visitation or beauty, and also as the grace of breath.

A visitation from on high came to the excellent and beautiful Church, giving the gift of the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, as referenced in john 4:14. The Church bore Christ a sojourning people, symbolized by Gershom, who are formed into beauty towards the Son. Those who are sealed with the divine Spirit and are worthy of heavenly visitation are sojourners in this world, recognizing their temporary presence here. It is fitting for them to cry out and say that they do not have a lasting city here, acknowledging their earthly pilgrimage.

The phrase 'visitation from on high' is reminiscent of Zechariah's song in Luke 1:68-79, but the exact reference is uncertain.
The word 'sojourners' is used to translate the Greek word πάροικοι, which refers to those who are temporary residents in a place.
